title: QueryFormer: Winning Solution for KDD Cup 2026 Tencent UniRec Challenge
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 15 Sep 2026]
    Title:QueryFormer: Winning Solution for KDD Cup 2026 Tencent UniRec Challenge
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:Post-click conversion rate (pCVR) prediction requires jointly modeling feature interactions and sequential user behaviors. The KDD Cup 2026 Tencent UniRec Challenge calls for a unified architecture addressing both. We observe that existing unified architectures often generate query tokens---the central information hub---with projection-based multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), without explicit token-to-query attention for refining the query side. We propose QueryFormer, centered on a stackable unified field--sequence block that bridges non-sequential multi-field features and behavioral sequences, and provide a latency-aware scaling study over view width $H$, model width, depth, data, and compute. The block generates queries through cross-attention and packs sequence queries into shared-parameter attention. QueryFormer secured 1st place in the Industrial Track, achieving an official test area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.83254; a modest post-competition scale-up reached 0.832713. Within our grid, $H$-scaling improves validation AUC from 0.84540 to 0.84615 and beats HyFormer at comparable budgets. Ablation identifies query generation as the largest contributor. Packed shared-parameter cross-attention keeps H=8 inference latency to only 1.89x that of H=1, positioning the bridge as an efficient stackable unified block.

report.summary: QueryFormer wins KDD Cup 2026 Tencent UniRec by using cross-attention to generate query tokens and unify feature interactions with user behavior sequences.
report.background: Post-click conversion rate prediction is central to online advertising and recommendation, requiring models to jointly capture multi-field feature interactions and sequential user behavior. The KDD Cup 2026 Tencent UniRec Challenge specifically asked for a unified architecture handling both. Many existing unified models generate query tokens—the central information hub—through projection-based MLPs, without explicit token-to-query attention to refine the query side. QueryFormer addresses this gap with a stackable unified field–sequence block that bridges non-sequential features and behavioral sequences. It also reports a latency-aware scaling study over view width, model width, depth, data, and compute, reflecting industrial concerns about accuracy and inference cost.
key_points: Query generation is the key innovation. Existing unified architectures create query tokens with projection MLPs, but QueryFormer generates queries through cross-attention, allowing sequence tokens to refine the central query representation. Ablation studies identify query generation as the largest single contributor to performance, suggesting that explicit token-to-query attention is more effective than simple projection for pCVR prediction.

The stackable unified field–sequence block bridges non-sequential multi-field features and behavioral sequences. It packs sequence queries into shared-parameter attention, enabling efficient stacking. This design lets the model jointly model feature interactions and sequential behavior without separate towers, which is precisely what the KDD Cup 2026 UniRec Challenge required.

QueryFormer won first place in the Industrial Track with an official test ROC AUC of 0.83254. A modest post-competition scale-up reached 0.832713. Within the authors' grid, H-scaling improved validation AUC from 0.84540 to 0.84615 and beat HyFormer at comparable compute budgets, indicating strong accuracy and generalization.

Latency-aware scaling shows efficiency. Packed shared-parameter cross-attention keeps inference latency at H=8 to only 1.89x that of H=1. This near-linear cost makes wider view configurations practical for industrial deployment, where real-time pCVR prediction must balance AUC gains against strict latency and compute constraints.

The paper provides a scaling study over view width H, model width, depth, data, and compute. Rather than reporting only a single winning configuration, it maps accuracy–latency trade-offs. This makes the bridge block a reusable component for teams seeking to scale unified recommendation or conversion models under production budgets.
report.impact: QueryFormer's win signals that unified architectures for pCVR and recommendation are moving toward attention-based query generation rather than MLP projections. For the AI industry, it validates cross-attention and shared-parameter packing as practical ways to combine feature and sequence modeling at scale. Developers can adopt these ideas in CTR/CVR pipelines, potentially improving AUC with controlled latency. Regular users may see more relevant ads and recommendations, since better conversion prediction can reduce irrelevant or mistimed content. However, gains depend on data quality, privacy constraints, and deployment costs, so teams should benchmark carefully before replacing existing production models.
report.tools: Follow arXiv:2609.16548 for the QueryFormer paper. Compare against the HyFormer baseline mentioned. Open-source CTR/CVR and recommendation libraries to test related ideas include DeepCTR, FuxiCTR, RecBole, TorchRec, Merlin HugeCTR, and TensorFlow Recommenders. For attention modules, PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers are useful. If QueryFormer code is released, check GitHub and KDD Cup 2026 UniRec resources for implementations and baselines.
